solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Women chop wood etc and bustle around locally

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for women
to hew is to chop wood or stone with an axe

explanation.surface: A busy woman splits logs and hurries about the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect sense: in northern English dialect, to whew is to bustle about.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives a dialect verb meaning to hurry or fuss about busily, which matches bustling around.

clue.text: Beardies mostly adorned fuzzily in tufts

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the following word is dropped
something seen fuzzily is blurred out of shape, so the letters lose their order
in places the jumbled letters inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a whisk is a small bunch or tuft, as of hay or feathers
the word with its final letter cut off

explanation.surface: Bearded men are mostly decorated with fuzzy tufts of hair.
explanation.walkthrough: WHISKERANDOS, from a whiskered Spanish character in Sheridan's The Critic, is a jocular word for whiskered men.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a person with bushy whiskers, so its plural describes bearded types, beardies.

clue.text: The lady's medium bust

blocks.note: the possessive pronoun for a woman
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A woman of average bust size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bust' looks like part of a dress fitting but means a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A herm is a square stone pillar topped with a sculpted head or bust, as of the god Hermes.

clue.text: * Embarrass

blocks.note: the asterisk marks the Azed competition word, for which solvers write their own clue
the setter supplies only a plain meaning: to hamper, hinder or weigh down

explanation.walkthrough: In an Azed competition puzzle one clue is replaced by a bare definition; readers send in clues for it, and this is that entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrass in its older sense means to hamper or impede, the same as to burden or hinder.

clue.text: Unseasoned sailor given instruction on being discharged

indicators.note: the little word on is let go, discharged from the word for instruction, leaving the rest

blocks.note: an old salt is a veteran sailor
a lesson is a period of instruction

explanation.surface: A raw recruit sailor gets his training as he is discharged from service.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON dropped is the final two letters of LESSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Food without salt has not been seasoned, so saltless is unseasoned, with a pun on salt meaning sailor.

clue.text: Treats for bears

blocks.note: first meaning: pays for someone, as in standing a round of drinks
second meaning: tolerates or puts up with

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests snacks for a zoo animal; both halves are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand someone a drink is to pay for it as a gift, and to stand something is to endure it.

clue.text: Like senior girl at lycée, student missing translator initially

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the letters for the translator are taken away
initially says the removed letters come off the front of the word

blocks.note: a trainee is someone still learning
tr. is the dictionary abbreviation for translator

explanation.surface: A description of an older schoolgirl at a French lycée whose student has lost her translator.
explanation.walkthrough: AINEE is French, used in English after a name to mean the elder sister.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective means elder, the feminine form, so it suits an older girl at a French school.

clue.text: It may be beside rug devouring scrap of chicken

definitions.text: It may be beside rug devouring scrap of chicken

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing up, so one piece goes inside another
a scrap is a small bit, here just the leading letter of the bird

blocks.note: to can mean close to, as in a door pulled to
a mat is a small rug
the opening letter of the bird

explanation.surface: A pet curled by the hearthrug tucking into a bit of chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the picture: the cat sat on, or beside, the mat.
explanation.definitionFit: A male cat is just the sort of animal found lying by a rug and eating scraps of chicken.

clue.text: Cunning delivery's last spinner tossed up

indicators.note: last picks out the final letter of the word before it
in a down entry, tossed up means the letters are read upwards, bottom to top

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
a reel is something that spins, as on a fishing rod

explanation.surface: A cricket bowler's crafty final ball is a spinner lobbed high.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of spin bowling hides a fishing reel. Besides wary, Chambers gives LEERY a slang sense of knowing or sly.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists a slang sense of knowing and sly, so a leery person is cunning as well as wary.

clue.text: Spades in resorts getting broken – cause of strain?

indicators.note: in puts the card suit inside the holiday places
broken means smashed apart, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bucket-and-spade holidays going wrong can be a source of tension.
explanation.walkthrough: The S goes into RESORTS before all eight letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stressor is any agent or event that puts a person or system under strain.

clue.text: Swinging crowd left in short session lacking a pastor?

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the shortened word
short shows the word for a sitting is cut down before it holds anything

blocks.note: hep is old slang for fashionable or swinging
a herd is a crowd, of people or animals
L is the abbreviation for left
the word with its last three letters cut off

explanation.surface: A lively crowd leaves a brief church meeting because there is no minister.
explanation.walkthrough: A pastor is literally a shepherd of his flock, which makes the question mark fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastor is Latin for shepherd and a priest tends a flock, so a congregation lacking one is shepherdless.

clue.text: Tossing the coin, tending towards reconciliation

indicators.note: tossing throws things about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Settling a dispute by flipping a coin, which leads to agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Henotic, from Greek for unifying, describes something that seeks to harmonise or reconcile opposing parties.

clue.text: Short book, one of E. European origin

blocks.note: first meaning: the abbreviation for the Old Testament Book of Esther
second meaning: Chambers gives the word as a name for an Estonian

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a slim volume by an émigré author.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the standard abbreviation of a Bible book and also an old term for a native of Estonia.

clue.text: Number encountered within earn terribly tiny measure

indicators.note: within puts the first pair of pieces inside the scrambled letters
terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters come out in disorder

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
to have met someone is to have encountered them
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone earning a pitifully small amount, measured in tiny sums.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a unit of length equal to a billionth of a metre, used for wavelengths and atoms.

clue.text: Sticks around, being rather too fond of oneself

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word is read from its end to its start

blocks.note: to gum something is to stick it with glue

explanation.surface: Someone sticks around, enjoying his own company too much.
explanation.definitionFit: Smugness is complacent self-satisfaction, an excessive pleasure in one's own merits.

clue.text: Ask what goes into late vehicles turning up

indicators.note: what goes into the words is the run of letters sitting inside them
in a down entry, turning up means the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: the letters across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A question about what goes into old cars as they arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ask' looks like a verb, but it is a dialect noun: an ask is a newt or lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old regional names for the newt or eft, so one serves to define the other.

clue.text: Fungus holding on in narrow passage

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: the cep is an edible mushroom, the porcino
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A mushroom clinging on inside a cramped tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers gives the noun a sense of a low tunnel or hole that animals or people crawl through.

clue.text: Love goddess scored, with narcotic drink around

indicators.note: around has the drink enclose the other word on both sides

blocks.note: kava is an intoxicating drink made from a Polynesian pepper root
to have made runs is to have scored them

explanation.surface: A goddess of love achieves her conquest with the help of a drug-laced drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Kamadeva is in fact a male Hindu god of love, so 'goddess' is slightly off.
explanation.definitionFit: Kamadeva is the Hindu deity of desire, often shown with a bow of sugarcane and arrows of flowers.

clue.text: Tub for dissolving salts heals throbbing pain mostly

indicators.note: throbbing means pulsing about, so the letters are moved into a new order
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A bath of salts soothes an aching pain, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests bath salts; the tub is for leaching lye from wood ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: An ash-leach is a vessel in which water is run through wood ashes to dissolve out the alkaline salts.

clue.text: Localized blow shows sandbank in its shifting form

indicators.note: in places the first word inside its own rearranged version
a shifting form keeps moving about, so the same letters reappear in a new order

blocks.note: Chambers has the Swedish ås, plural åsar, for a ridge of sand or gravel, an esker
its refers back to the same sandbank word

explanation.surface: A local word for a blow involving a sandbank whose shape keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: The sandbank word goes inside a rearrangement of itself. The clue uses the plural form for a single sandbank. 'Localized' marks a dialect word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers lists it as a dialect variant of siserary, meaning a sharp blow or a scolding.

clue.text: Nervous wreck when beset by withering beaks etc (2 words)

indicators.note: withering suggests shrivelling out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
beset by means surrounded, so the little word sits inside the others

blocks.note: taken as written
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone goes to pieces when surrounded by scornful magistrates and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaks' is British slang for magistrates or headmasters, which suits the picture of a cowering wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket case is an informal term for someone too anxious or stressed to function.

clue.text: African chief, one taken in by hoax

indicators.note: taken in by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to kid is to fool or hoax someone
a means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A chief in Africa is duped by a trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaid, or caid, is a North African chief, governor or commander.

clue.text: Nasty pains I cast off after rhubarb

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Rheum is the botanical genus of rhubarb
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has thrown off painful aches after eating rhubarb.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: RHEUM comes first, with the shuffled letters after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheumatics is an informal name for the aches and pains of rheumatism in muscles and joints.

clue.text: White man in Zambia scattered gnu in frenzy throwing stone

indicators.note: scattered means spread about, so the animal's letters come out in another order
in places the scrambled animal inside the shortened frenzy word
throwing means casting away, so the letters for the weight are discarded

blocks.note: Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia
must, or musth, is the frenzied state of a male elephant in rut
taken as written
st is the abbreviation for stone, the weight

explanation.surface: A white man in Zambia scatters wild gnus as he hurls stones in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Z is Zambia's international vehicle code. The word is Swahili, heard more in Kenya and Tanzania than in Zambia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mzungu is the Bantu term in eastern and central Africa for a white person or European.

clue.text: Ill-conceived, is born in poetic circles

indicators.note: something ill-conceived is badly formed, so the letters are put together wrongly

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A badly planned child is born into literary society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poetic circles' looks like a literary set; it is a poetic verb meaning encircles.
explanation.definitionFit: Milton's verb inorb means to set in an orb or encircle, so it is a poet's word for circles.

clue.text: Eager to be found in poetry of yesteryear? Sounds fishy

definitions.text: Eager to be found in poetry of yesteryear

indicators.note: sounds tells us to go by how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: the bream is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone keen to appear in old verse finds the whole thing suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: BREEM, or breme, is a Spenserian word meaning fierce or keen, hence old poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser and older poets used the word for keen or fierce, which fits eager in archaic verse.

clue.text: On being embraced by wizard totty, heading for heaven

indicators.note: being embraced means held inside, so the little word goes into the other
in Scots, totty means dizzy or unsteady, so the letters are tottered out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wrapped in the arms of a sexy wizard, someone is in heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totty' looks like British slang for an attractive woman; here it is the Scots adjective for unsteady.
explanation.definitionFit: Zion stands for heaven in hymns, and the suffix -ward means towards, so it means going heavenwards.

clue.text: Belt supporting middle of abdomen? It's bracing

indicators.note: middle picks out the central letter of the word that follows
in a down entry, supporting means sitting underneath, so the belt goes below

blocks.note: the central letter of the seven
a zone was originally a girdle or belt

explanation.surface: A support belt for the stomach, praised for being firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bracing' looks like the belt giving support but means refreshing, as seaside air.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is popularly used for the fresh, invigorating air of the seaside, so it is something bracing.

clue.text: Erstwhile statesman? He's where ashes are returned

indicators.note: saying he is where something is kept places him inside it
returned means sent back, so the combined letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: taken as written
an urn is where cremated ashes are kept

explanation.surface: A former statesman, now cremated, is where his ashes lie.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a vague hint; the whole clue also pictures the cremated Nehru.
explanation.definitionFit: Jawaharlal Nehru was India's first prime minister, and he was cremated after his death in 1964.

clue.text: Origin of forces in sci-fi volume right and left I absorbed

indicators.note: absorbed means soaked up inside, so the single letter goes within the others

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for volume
R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A science fiction book cites the source of its powers.
explanation.definitionFit: Vril is the mysterious energy source of a subterranean race in Bulwer-Lytton's novel The Coming Race.

clue.text: Each Scotch stimulated alkie endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped
stimulated suggests stirred up, so the letters are moved about

blocks.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: Every glass of whisky perks up a drinker without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but marks a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilka is the Scots word for every or each, as in Burns's 'ilka lassie'.

clue.text: Rabbi's to recite prayers having left desk

blocks.note: to daven is the Yiddish verb for reciting Jewish prayers
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: A rabbi must pray before leaving his desk.
explanation.definitionFit: A davenport is a small writing desk with a sloping top and drawers, named after its first customer.

clue.text: Response when changing ends? It should not be overstepped

indicators.note: changing ends means the first and last letters trade places

blocks.note: an echo is a sound returned in response

explanation.surface: A question about what reply comes when teams swap sides, then a warning about a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The oche is the line a darts player stands behind when throwing.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts, a player's toes must stay behind the oche, so it is a line not to be crossed.

clue.text: Strips in the woods? Sunk with bra getting twisted

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the letters are wrung into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone strips naked in the forest, bra twisted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips' suggests undressing; here it is the stripping of bark from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbark a tree is to strip off its bark, something done in woodland.

clue.text: Impostor exercises gumshoes

blocks.note: a sham is a fake or impostor
to exercise a right is to use it

explanation.surface: A fraud keeps private investigators busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamus and gumshoe are both American slang for a private detective.

clue.text: 'The car is back'? Such may be heard among the Cotswolds

definitions.text: Such may be heard among the Cotswolds

indicators.note: back tells us the brand name is read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: Saab is a Swedish car make

explanation.surface: Someone announces a car's return; such noises carry in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are hills in western England, but Cotswold is also a breed of sheep, hence bleats.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleating sheep make the sound, so it is what would be heard among a flock of Cotswold sheep.
